query: Is Gasherbrum II or Nuptse closest to the tallest mountain in the world?
ground_truth: It lies two kilometres WSW of Mount Everest.

pipeline_result.response: Nuptse is closer to the highest mountain on Earth, Mount Everest (8611 m), than it is to the tallest mountain in the world, Mount Tongshanjiabu.
retrieved_context: Nuptse: Nuptse or Nubtse (Sherpa: ནུབ་རྩེ། नुबचे, Wylie: Nub rtse) is a mountain in the Khumbu region of the Mahalangur Himal, in the Nepalese Himalayas.  It lies two kilometres WSW of Mount Everest.  Nubtse is Tibetan for "west peak", as it is the western segment of the Lhotse-Nubtse massif.

South Summit (Mount Everest): The South Summit of Mount Everest in the Himalayas is the second-highest peak on Earth, and is a subsidiary peak to the primary peak of Mount Everest.  Although its elevation above sea level of 8749 m is higher than the second-highest mountain on Earth, K2 (whose summit is 8611 m above sea level), it is only considered a separate peak and not a separate mountain as its prominence is only 11 meters.

Tongshanjiabu: Tongshanjiabu () is a mountain in the Himalayas.  At 7,207 m tall, Tongshanjiabu is the 103rd tallest mountain in the world.  It sits in the disputed border territory between Bhutan and China.  Tongshanjiabu has never been officially climbed.
